context.process_name: Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance
context.objective: Document how we carry out Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?

It kicks off when new money comes into a fund that has already been going for a while. So either a brand new investor gets let in, or somebody who is already in the fund decides to put in more. At that point we sort of true everyone up so the newcomer is on the same footing as the people who were there from the start.
Talk me through how you handle the equalization and rebalance once a new or additional investment comes in?

Sure, roughly speaking. We open up the close and make sure the investor is actually ready to come in. Then we pin down what the fund's partnership agreement says about how the catch-up is supposed to work, because it is different fund to fund. After that we go back through the earlier capital calls and work out what the new investor would have put in if they had been there all along, and we put interest on top of that. We figure out how that interest gets shared among the investors who were already in. Then a call goes out to the new investor for the catch-up amount. Once that is done we redo everybody's percentages going forward, and at the end we update the books and reconcile everything so the close can be shut.
What information from the earlier calls and the partnership agreement determines the catch-up and interest amounts?

From the earlier calls we need every capital call that happened before the investor's admission or effective date, and for each one the call date, the total base, what it was for, and how much each existing investor funded. From the partnership agreement, the LPA, plus any side letters, we take which part of each earlier call counts, the interest rate, the start and end dates, the day-count and accrual basis, whether it compounds, and who the interest goes to and how it is treated. The catch-up capital itself is the investor's approved commitment percentage times the included amount of each prior call, after any exclusions the fund's documents require. Interest then runs on each of those, call by call, from the original funding date to the admission or effective date. We never assume the day count, simple versus compound, or who receives it. That all has to come from the LPA.
How do you check that the catch-up and interest calculations are correct before the call goes out?
Mostly a second person goes over it, and we make sure the numbers all tie out before anything goes out the door. If something does not tie, the call just does not get released until it is sorted.
What do you compare the calculated amounts against when you tie them out?

A few things. The list of earlier calls and what each investor funded gets reconciled to the prior notices, the historical contribution records, the general ledger and trial balance, and the capital accounts, and there has to be zero unexplained difference. For the catch-up capital, the call-by-call detail has to add up to the total, and the percentage and the call base have to trace back to the executed commitments and approved inputs. For interest, the second reviewer independently recalculates it and checks the dates, rate, basis, compounding, formula and total against the method in the LPA. The interest we allocate out to the existing investors has to equal the total interest, with no leftover. And the notice itself, meaning the backdated capital, interest, fee and total due on it, has to agree to the approved schedules before it is released.
How do you determine each existing investor’s share of the interest?

It depends on the fund. I identify which existing investors are entitled to be compensated and the allocation basis the LPA sets, and then allocate the interest investor by investor on that basis. Then I apply whatever treatment the LPA requires, which can be a cash payment to them, an addition to their capital accounts, or some other approved mechanism. If any investor is excluded or gets special treatment, I document why. If it is unclear who should receive the interest, or whether it is cash or capital, I escalate it and the client or their legal counsel decides. I do not pick one myself. I could not give you one formula that works for every fund. There is supposed to be a fund-by-fund register of those LPA rules, but I do not know where that stands. Someone on the legal or governing-documents side would have to confirm it.
When you say “once that is done,” what has happened with the catch-up call?

By that point the call has been put together and sent. I assemble the new investor's backdated capital, the equalization interest, the management-fee catch-up if one applies, and any other approved component. I populate the allocation and notice data, and the notice shows each component separately plus the total due. It goes through internal review and the client approves it, and that part runs through our regular capital call process, which we call FA-01. The FA-01 team is the one that actually releases the notice. After that the funding is tracked through the cash application process, FA-02. The receipts themselves get reconciled at the very end, when we close out.
How do you recalculate each investor’s going-forward percentage after the new or additional commitment is included?

I recalculate the fund's total commitments after the close, using the executed post-close commitments, and then work out each investor's percentage of that for future events. I do not just reuse the old percentages sitting in Excel. I recalculate both the pre-close and the post-close totals. Where earlier investments keep different economics, which happens in deal-by-deal funds, I leave those investment-specific historical percentages as they are and do not overwrite them. Every schedule gets its effective date recorded. All of that lives in the commitment and ownership schedule and the Excel allocation engine. Then I update the inputs for future capital calls, distributions, the waterfall and reporting. The percentages have to reconcile to the approved commitments and add up to the required total, apart from documented exclusions or rounding, and the second reviewer has to approve them before the next event.
What tells you the investor is ready to be included in the close?

A few things have to be in place. I need the client's close notification and the executed subscription document, or the commitment-increase paperwork if it is an existing investor putting in more, and onboarding and the anti-money-laundering checks have to be finished. I confirm the client has approved the admission, that AML has cleared, and where the system and portal setup stands. I record it in the close checklist: the fund, the investor, the close or effective date, the commitment, and whether it is a new admission or an upsize. At the same time I assign a second reviewer, flag any legal, tax, management-fee or accounting dependencies, and set the completion date so it lands before the investor's next capital activity. If documents are incomplete, or the AML, commitment or effective-date records are missing, I escalate. No equalization call gets released for an investor who is not approved and cleared.
How does the close team learn that a new admission or commitment increase is coming?

Like I mentioned, it comes from the client. They send us a close notification, and the client is the one who confirms the admission date and the commitment. There is no fixed schedule for it. It is event-driven, and it can happen more than once while the fund is still fundraising. Investor Services is involved as well, since they confirm the onboarding, and they will hold the investor's participation or the notice if onboarding or the portal setup is not complete.
How does Investor Services let you know when onboarding and portal setup are complete so the hold can be lifted?

The second reviewer independently recalculates interest and checks dates, rate, basis, compounding, formula and total against the LPA. Allocated interest must equal total interest with no leftover. Compare notice capital, interest, fee and total to approved schedules before release. The relationship to the separate internal notice review is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Hold call for tie-out issue
steps.description: Do not release the call while a tie-out issue remains unresolved. How the issue is sorted and where work resumes are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Apply interest treatment
steps.description: Apply the LPA-required treatment after allocation: cash payment, addition to capital accounts or another approved mechanism. Its timing relative to notice and close-out work is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Escalate unclear interest rules
steps.description: Escalate uncertainty about interest recipients or whether treatment is cash or capital; the participant does not choose the answer.

steps.title: Decide unclear interest treatment
steps.description: Decide the escalated question about recipients or cash-versus-capital treatment. Recording and resumption are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Assemble catch-up notice
steps.description: Assemble backdated capital, equalization interest, any applicable management-fee catch-up and other approved components. Populate allocation and notice data; show each component separately and the total due.

steps.title: Complete internal notice review
steps.description: The notice goes through internal review in FA-01. Its relationship to the calculation and notice tie-outs, review content and order relative to client approval are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Approve catch-up notice
steps.description: The client approves the notice in FA-01. Approval criteria and rejection or delay handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Track catch-up funding
steps.description: After notice release, track funding through cash application process FA-02. Receipts are reconciled at close-out; the immediate handoff is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Approve recalculated percentages
steps.description: Approve the recalculated percentages before the next event. Specific checks and rejection handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Update future-event inputs
steps.description: Update inputs for future capital calls, distributions, the waterfall and reporting after recalculating percentages. Timing relative to percentage approval is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Record the close checklist
steps.description: Record fund, investor, close or effective date, commitment, and whether the event is a new admission or upsize.

steps.title: Assign reviewer and flag dependencies
steps.description: At the same time as checklist recording, assign a second reviewer, flag legal, tax, management-fee or accounting dependencies, and set a completion date before the investor's next capital activity.

steps.title: Escalate missing readiness items
steps.description: Escalate incomplete documents or missing AML, commitment or effective-date records. Recipient, resolution and return route are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm investor onboarding
steps.description: Investor Services confirms onboarding. The confirmation's handoff and exact placement relative to the readiness check are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Hold participation or notice
steps.description: Hold investor participation or the notice if onboarding or portal setup is incomplete. The release signal and subsequent handoff are UNKNOWN.

topics.answer: The intake names the work Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance. It includes investor catch-up, interest allocation, notice, ownership rebalance and close-out.
True up investors so a newcomer is on the same footing as those in the fund from the start.

The client sends the participant's team a close notification for a new admission or commitment increase and confirms the admission date and commitment.
The work is event-driven, without a fixed schedule, and may recur during fundraising.
The participant sets a completion date before the investor's next capital activity.
Investor readiness requires the executed subscription or commitment-increase paperwork, completed onboarding and AML checks, and client approval of the admission; the participant also checks the system and portal setup status.
The books are updated and everything reconciled so the close can be shut; receipts are reconciled at the very end. Detailed close-out criteria, closure evidence and downstream consumer are UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN: the role accountable for the overall result has not been identified.

Open the close and check investor readiness; determine fund rules; calculate prior-call catch-up and interest; and allocate interest. The participant applies the required treatment, but its timing relative to notice and close-out is UNKNOWN. The participant assembles the notice, which goes through FA-01 review and client approval before release; FA-02 tracks funding. After the notice is sent, the participant recalculates commitment totals and future ownership percentages, preserves applicable deal-specific historical percentages and updates future-event inputs. Books are updated and everything, including receipts, is reconciled at close-out. The participant records a checklist, assigns a reviewer and flags dependencies; Investor Services confirms onboarding and may hold participation or the notice. Missing readiness items, unclear interest rules and failed tie-outs have reported escalation or hold paths, but their returns and several handoffs are UNKNOWN.

Mostly a second person reviews calculations. Historical calls and funding reconcile to notices, contribution records, ledger, trial balance and capital accounts with zero unexplained difference. Catch-up detail and inputs must trace and add up; a second reviewer independently recalculates interest; allocations must equal total interest; and notice amounts must match approved schedules. Mismatches hold release. Internal review and client notice approval precede FA-01 release; investor approval and AML clearance are also required. Investor Services holds participation or the notice if onboarding or portal setup is incomplete. Revised percentages reconcile to commitments and need second-reviewer approval before the next event. Review order, detailed responsibilities, retained evidence and rejection or rework routes remain UNKNOWN.

New admissions use subscription documents; commitment increases use increase paperwork. Fund documents vary the included calls, interest terms, recipients and treatment; cash, capital-account additions or another approved mechanism are possible. In deal-by-deal funds, investment-specific historical percentages remain unchanged where earlier economics differ. Effort, charging, removal constraints and whether these share the same process boundary are UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN: no specific friction, manual-work burden or practical effect was reported.
UNKNOWN: material failure consequences were not described.

Reported materials include the LPA and any side letters, prior notices and contribution records, ledger and capital accounts, executed commitments, approved inputs and schedules, the investor notice, close checklist, commitment and ownership schedule and Excel allocation engine. A fund-by-fund LPA rules register is supposed to exist, but its status and location are UNKNOWN. No documents were supplied for review.

The work concerns an already operating fund and either a new investor or an existing investor increasing a commitment. Fund-specific rules and deal-by-deal economics change the work. General GPFS versus client-specific applicability and the overall parent-process boundary are UNKNOWN.

The participant reports that the LPA and side letters supply call inclusion and interest terms. Catch-up capital is approved commitment percentage times the included amount of each earlier call after exclusions; interest runs call by call from original funding to admission or effective date. The LPA determines entitled investors, allocation basis and treatment; the client or legal counsel decides unclear recipient or cash-versus-capital questions. Future percentages use executed post-close commitments, with specified historical percentages preserved. Source conflict authority, recorded interpretations, rounding and correction mechanics remain UNKNOWN; documents were not reviewed.

The client supplies the notification and approves admission and the notice. Onboarding and AML completion are readiness dependencies; Investor Services confirms onboarding. FA-01 handles notice review, approval and release, and FA-02 tracks subsequent funding. Future capital calls, distributions, waterfall and reporting receive updated inputs. Handoff mechanics, other dependencies and the final downstream consumer are UNKNOWN.

Inputs include prior-call dates, bases, purposes and investor funding, approved commitment percentages and fund rules. The participant recalculates ownership rather than reusing old Excel percentages; the commitment and ownership schedule and Excel allocation engine hold the resulting information. System and portal setup are checked but not named. Authoritative records, calculation locations for catch-up and interest, entry modes and storage are UNKNOWN.
There is no fixed schedule, and subsequent closes can occur more than once during fundraising. Counts, peaks, exception frequency and effort by step are UNKNOWN.
